name: ExLlamaV2 EXL2 kernel throughput benchmarks (3090 Ti / 4090)
activation_scheme: FP16 activations, no quantization. Weights are quantized to mixed bit widths (2-8 bits) with per-group scales. The kernel dequantizes to FP16 before the multiply.
notes: GROUP SIZE LEFT NULL 2026-10-04 for the same reason as the exl2 record LEFT NULL 2026-10-04 for the same reason as the exl2 record: EXL2's mixed per-tensor bitrate has no single group size. ExLlamaV2 throughput benchmarks from the README (3090 Ti / 4090): Llama GPTQ 7B grpsz 128: 181/205 t/s. Llama GPTQ 13B grpsz 128: 110/114 t/s. Llama GPTQ 33B grpsz 128 act-order: 44/48 t/s. OpenLlama GPTQ 3B grpsz 128 act-order: 259/296 t/s. CodeLlama EXL2 4.0 bpw 34B: 44/50 t/s. Llama2 EXL2 3.0 bpw 7B: 217/257 t/s. Llama2 EXL2 4.0 bpw 7B: 185/211 t/s. Llama2 EXL2 5.0 bpw 7B: 164/179 t/s. Llama2 EXL2 2.5 bpw 70B: 33/38 t/s. TinyLlama EXL2 3.0 bpw 1.1B: 656/770 t/s. TinyLlama EXL2 4.0 bpw 1.1B: 602/700 t/s. KEY OBSERVATION: The throughput scales inversely with bit width - 2.5 bpw is slower than 3.0 bpw which is slower than 4.0 bpw. This is because lower bit widths require more complex dequantization and the memory bandwidth saving is offset by increased compute overhead. The 70B model at 2.5 bpw runs at 33-38 t/s, which is usable but much slower than the 7B model at 4.0 bpw (185-211 t/s). The act-order flag (activation-aware ordering) improves quality but reduces throughput. No quality delta is published in the README - only throughput numbers. The project is archived with development moved to ExLlamaV3.
